source: Fux, The Study of Counterpoint (trans. Mann, 1965), pp. 78-79, Fig. 102: Joseph's rewrite of bars 7-11 of Fig. 101, the bass rising to the high C
transcription: Sounding pitches as MIDI numbers, durations in beats (a whole note is 4), from bar 7 (six bars' rest first, so the bars keep Fux's numbers); a third number is a note's written degree (C major's degrees, 0 = C4). Voices top to bottom: the cantus, the tenor, the bass. Aloys's verdict (p. 79): 'two progressions of the same kind follow immediately; from the ninth bar to the tenth, and from the tenth bar to the last' (hidden fifths and octaves), and in bar 9 the tenor and bass 'blend in a unison'.
